sections.title: The letter I
paragraphs: The letter name is (I) /iː/. Its main sound is a short vowel, as in (Insel) /ˈɪnzl̩/, which means island. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter makes three sounds in German words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, push your tongue forward and keep your lips relaxed. For the next sound, raise your tongue higher and spread your lips wide into a smile. For the last sound, raise the tongue close to the hard roof of the mouth and let the voice glide into the next sound. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake on each sound.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In closed syllables before two consonants, the letter sounds short, as in (bitte) /ˈbɪtə/. In open syllables with stress, it sounds long, as in (Tiger) /ˈtiːɡɐ/. Before another vowel in borrowed words, it sounds like an approximant, as in (Familie) /faˈmiːli̯ə/. An approximant is a consonant where the mouth gets close but air still flows smoothly.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not replace the long vowel with the sound in bit. Spread your lips wide and hold the vowel steady, as in English see. In words like (Igel) /ˈiːɡl̩/, keep the sound long and pure without gliding into another vowel.
